## Overview

Adds `--kv-cache-dtype mxfp4` with `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'` for MiniMax-M3.1 on ROCm gfx950 (MI355X, TP4): K, V and the indexer's key cache are stored as MXFP4 (e2m1 values, one e8m0 scale per 32), 68 B per token and head. Reference implementation: [ROCm/ATOM#2770](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2770).

**Draft; not runnable yet.** #64111 has merged, so this is now rebased onto main (`16d667348d`) as 5 commits (4 feature commits plus a test-only type fix). It still waits on three open AITER PRs (#7056, #7060, #7061), merged #7057, and an AITER pin bump (see Details). Placeholder to claim the work and get early design feedback.

AI-assisted (Claude Code). No human has reviewed the diff line by line yet; this stays a draft until that is done.

## Claims

- New cache dtype `mxfp4` (uint8 storage, `KVQuantMode.MXFP4`) and a gfx950 attend for MiniMax-M3 sparse attention. Per head a 128-token page is `[128 x 64 B e2m1][128 x 4 B e8m0]` = 8704 B; the main K/V spec is `num_head_slots=2*Hkv, state_content_bytes=68`, the index spec `head_size=68`.
- The fused QK-norm / RoPE kernel (AITER `fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm`) writes the MXFP4 K, V and index-K pages and writes the main q as e4m3 into `q_out`.
- Index scores come from AITER's FlyDSL MXFP4 scorers (decode and prefill); the top-k is the one the NVFP4 indexer uses; the attend runs AITER's `pa_decode_mxfp4` on a one-block-per-page table, for decode and prefill.
- The MXFP4 decode scorer's work map is one persistent buffer built for the model-length block bound, so FULL decode CUDA graphs replay a valid map.
- Not covered: Mono decode (stays off), indexer CP, TP other than 4, the MTP/DSpark draft layers (the existing check raises).

## Validation

Rebased onto main `16d667348d` (live main tip when this was pushed); `git range-diff` against the previous head `d24ae8f7f2` shows the 4 feature commits patch-identical; the 5th commit (`d6dbccaac4`) only touches `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_mxfp4_kv_cache.py`. Checked on a CPU-only host, no GPU used:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `pytest tests/models/minimax_m3/test_mxfp4_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_mxfp4.py` | 9 passed, 1 skipped (the kernel test file skips: needs gfx950 FlyDSL kernels) |
| `pre-commit run` (all hooks, including mypy) on the 14 changed files, at `d6dbccaac4` | pass. The earlier head `ffd9f4a06d` had 3 mypy errors in `tests/models/minimax_m3/test_mxfp4_kv_cache.py` (dynamic attributes on the fake aiter module, an Optional `decode.max_seq_len`); fixed in the 5th commit by typing the fake module as `Any` and asserting `decode is not None`, assertions unchanged. |

**CI at `d6dbccaac4`:** pre-commit and pre-run-check pass; docs build was still pending when this was written.

**Not validated after the rebase: any GPU run.** The kernel tests, end-to-end serving, CUDA-graph capture, accuracy and speed were not re-run on this head. Results quoted in earlier versions of this description were measured on the pre-rebase head `d24ae8f7f2` on an ROCm image and are not repeated as evidence for this head. CI has no gfx950 job that can run these ops: the kernel tests skip until the AITER pin carries them.

For orientation only, ATOM's own measurements of the same kernels (ATOM#2770, MiniMax-M3.1 TP4, MXFP4 KV and index against the NVFP4 path): c32 +7.4% throughput and +26.2% P90 interactivity, c48 +8.1% and +32.3%; KV capacity 13.4M against 7.3M tokens for fp8. These are ATOM results, not vLLM results.

## Details

**Prerequisites.** ROCm/aiter#7057 (fused write kernel: MXFP4 K/V and index-K, e4m3 `q_out`; this PR follows its final API, in which `q_fp8_out` and `q_scale` are gone) has merged; the remaining ROCm/aiter#7056 (FlyDSL `pa_decode_mxfp4`), #7060 (index decode scorer) and #7061 (index prefill scorers) need to merge, then an AITER pin bump in `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base`, then this PR. The pin is not bumped here. AITER is imported inside functions behind `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`; without the ops the layer raises a message naming those PRs.

**Commits** (on `16d667348d`):
1. `99556ddca5` Add the mxfp4 KV cache dtype and its page geometry (no behavior change on its own)
2. `507ac36aef` MXFP4 K/V and index cache on gfx950 (indexer, attend, write, tests, docs)
3. `06fdab1145` Pass the e4m3 main q as `q_out` to the aiter MXFP4 write
4. `ffd9f4a06d` Keep the MXFP4 decode work map stable for CUDA-graph replay
5. `d6dbccaac4` Fix mypy errors in `test_mxfp4_kv_cache.py` (test-only)

**Why not a duplicate.** No open or merged PR stores MiniMax-M3 K/V or index keys as MXFP4. #63547 is fp8 KV, #45838 is MXFP4 experts, #59739 (`mxfp4_mla`) and #64120 (`mxfp4_ds_mla`) are MLA/DSv4 caches. The dtype string `mxfp4` is a distinct exact-match name from `mxfp4_mla` and `mxfp4_ds_mla`; `KVQuantMode.MXFP4 = 16` avoids the 15 #64120 takes.

**Design.**
- It mirrors the NVFP4 hooks (`is_mxfp4` dispatch in `amd/model.py`, a sibling indexer and sparse backend), and reuses its metadata builders, FlyDSL top-k and the existing `sparse_pa` block-table kernels, which gain a `pages_per_block` argument (1 for a page-128 cache).
- AITER's `pa_sparse_block_topk` is not used: its build only accepts `pages_per_block == 8`, and it expects scores already pinned by the scorer, which the MXFP4 scorers do not do. A small Triton kernel writes AITER's init/local sentinels (1e30 / 1e29) on each row's causal blocks, and the existing top-k reads only a row's causal blocks, so the scorer's unwritten entries are never seen.
- The index query is bf16 and the main query e4m3 (the configuration ATOM measured).
- It needs one KV head per rank (TP4 on the 4-KV-head checkpoint); the checks raise a message with the reason otherwise.

**Size.** About 850 lines of non-test code, most of it the two new files (`indexer_mxfp4.py`, `sparse_attention_mxfp4.py`) that parallel the NVFP4 ones, plus about 700 lines of tests. Docs: one line in `docs/features/quantization/quantized_kvcache.md`.

@@ -39,6 +39,7 @@ You can configure how the quantization scales are computed in vLLM using three d
 - `kv_cache_dtype="auto"`: Use the model's default data type
 - `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e4m3"`: Supported on CUDA 11.8+ and ROCm (AMD GPUs)
 - `kv_cache_dtype="fp8_e5m2"`: Supported on CUDA 11.8+
+- `kv_cache_dtype="mxfp4"`: MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on ROCm gfx950 (MI350 and MI355X). K, V and the indexer's key cache are stored as MXFP4 (e2m1 values with one e8m0 scale per 32 values), 68 bytes per token and head against 128 for fp8. It needs `--attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4"}'`, `--block-size 128`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1` with an AITER that has the MXFP4 FlyDSL ops, and tensor parallel size 4 (one KV head per rank).
 
 ### Skipping Specific Layers from KV-Cache Quantization

@@ -0,0 +1,544 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 K/V and index cache on ROCm gfx950: the fused write, the
+index scores + top-k and the sparse attend, each against a torch reference on
+the dequantized pages.
+
+Needs VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 and an aiter with the MXFP4 FlyDSL ops
+(ROCm/aiter#7056, #7057, #7060, #7061).
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers import PreTrainedConfig
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+    pytest.skip("ROCm (gfx950) FlyDSL kernels", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm.platforms.rocm import on_gfx950  # noqa: E402
+
+if not on_gfx950():
+    pytest.skip("gfx950 instructions", allow_module_level=True)
+
+from vllm._aiter_ops import rocm_aiter_ops  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.indexer_mxfp4 import (  # noqa: E402
+    _pin_forced_blocks,
+    mxfp4_index_topk_decode,
+    mxfp4_index_topk_prefill,
+    rocm_mxfp4_aiter_unavailable_reason,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.model import (  # noqa: E402
+    MiniMAXGemmaRMSNorm,
+    MiniMaxM3SparseAttention,
+    _build_rotary_emb,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.mxfp4_pages import (  # noqa: E402
+    PAGE_BYTES,
+    mxfp4_page_views,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.sparse_pa import (  # noqa: E402
+    minimax_m3_build_sparse_block_table_decode,
+    minimax_m3_build_sparse_block_table_prefill,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.sparse_attention_mxfp4 import (  # noqa: E402
+    mxfp4_sparse_attend,
+)
+from vllm.models.minimax_m3.common.sparse_attention import (  # noqa: E402
+    minimax_m3_query_token_positions,
+)
+
+reason = rocm_mxfp4_aiter_unavailable_reason()
+if reason is not None:
+    pytest.skip(f"MXFP4 ops: {reason}", allow_module_level=True)
+
+BLOCK = 128
+D = 128
+TOPK = 16
+NQ = 16  # query heads per rank at TP4
+ROT = 64
+SCALE = D**-0.5
+SENTINEL = 0xA5
+SLACK = 0.04
+E2M1 = (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0)
+
+
+def quantize_pages(rows: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """uint8 pages ``[P, 8704]`` of float rows ``[P, 128, 128]``: per 32 values
+    the e8m0 scale ceil_pow2(amax / 6) and the nearest e2m1 code."""
+    x = rows.float().unflatten(-1, (4, 32))
+    amax = x.abs().amax(-1).clamp_min(2.0**-100)
+    exp = torch.ceil(torch.log2(amax / 6.0)).clamp(-100, 100)
+    y = x / torch.exp2(exp)[..., None]
+    grid = torch.tensor(E2M1, device=rows.device)
+    code = (y.abs()[..., None] - grid).abs().argmin(-1) | ((y < 0) << 3)
+    code = code.flatten(-2)
+    data = (code[..., 0::2] | (code[..., 1::2] << 4)).to(torch.uint8)
+    scale = (exp + 127).to(torch.uint8)
+    p = rows.shape[0]
+    return torch.cat([data.reshape(p, -1), scale.reshape(p, -1)], dim=-1)
+
+
+def dequantize_pages(pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """float32 rows ``[..., 128, 128]`` of uint8 pages ``[..., 8704]``."""
+    data, scale = mxfp4_page_views(pages)
+    d = data.int()
+    code = torch.stack((d & 15, d >> 4), dim=-1).flatten(-2)
+    grid = torch.tensor(E2M1, device=pages.device)
+    value = grid[code & 7] * torch.where(code & 8 != 0, -1.0, 1.0)
+    step = torch.exp2(scale.float() - 127.0)[..., None]
+    return (value.unflatten(-1, (4, 32)) * step).flatten(-2)
+
+
+def group_steps(pages: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Per-element value of one e8m0 step, ``[..., 128, 128]``."""
+    _, scale = mxfp4_page_views(pages)
+    step = torch.exp2(scale.float() - 127.0)
+    return step.repeat_interleave(32, dim=-1)
+
+
+def block_table(seq_lens, extra=2, seed=0):
+    widths = [-(-s // BLOCK) for s in seq_lens]
+    num_pages = sum(widths) + extra
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    perm = torch.randperm(num_pages, device="cuda", generator=g).to(torch.int32)
+    table = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens), max(widths), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    start = 0
+    for r, w in enumerate(widths):
+        table[r, :w] = perm[start : start + w]
+        start += w
+    return table, num_pages
+
+
+# ---- the fused write -------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _write_inputs(num_tokens, dtype=torch.bfloat16, seed=0):
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    row = (NQ + 2 + 1 + 1) * D
+    qkv = torch.randn(num_tokens, row, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", generator=g)
+    w = (torch.randn(D, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", generator=g) * 0.1).to(dtype)
+    cos_sin = torch.randn(
+        max(num_tokens, 64), ROT, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", generator=g
+    )
+    return qkv, w, cos_sin, torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 7, 300, 1031])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("skip_index", [False, True])
+def test_write_matches_bf16_cache(num_tokens, skip_index):
+    """K, V, index-K and the e4m3 q written through the vLLM wrapper are the
+    bf16 rows of the "auto" cache to within one e8m0 step of their group."""
+    import aiter
+
+    qkv, w, cos_sin, pos = _write_inputs(num_tokens, seed=num_tokens)
+    slots = torch.randperm(((num_tokens + 127) // 128 + 1) * 128, device="cuda")
+    slots = slots[:num_tokens].to(torch.int64)
+    if num_tokens > 5:
+        slots[::5] = -1
+    num_pages = (int(slots.max()) + 128) // 128 + 1
+
+    k_ref = torch.zeros(num_pages, 128, 1, D, dtype=qkv.dtype, device="cuda")
+    v_ref = torch.zeros_like(k_ref)
+    i_ref = torch.zeros(num_pages, 128, D, dtype=qkv.dtype, device="cuda")
+    q_ref = torch.empty(num_tokens, NQ * D, dtype=qkv.dtype, device="cuda")
+    iq_ref = torch.empty(num_tokens, D, dtype=qkv.dtype, device="cuda")
+    aiter.fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm(

+@triton.jit
+def _pin_forced_blocks_kernel(
+    score_ptr,  # [H, rows, width] fp32
+    seq_lens_ptr,  # decode: [num_reqs]
+    num_valid_ptr,  # prefill: [rows] causal block count of each row
+    stride_h,
+    stride_row,
+    query_len,
+    init_blocks,
+    local_blocks,
+    DECODE: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    SENTINEL_INIT: tl.constexpr,
+    SENTINEL_LOCAL: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    head = tl.program_id(1)
+    if DECODE:
+        seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + row // query_len)
+        kv_len = tl.maximum(seq_len - query_len + row % query_len + 1, 0)
+        num_blocks = (kv_len + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) // BLOCK_SIZE
+    else:
+        num_blocks = tl.load(num_valid_ptr + row)
+    score_row = score_ptr + head.to(tl.int64) * stride_h + row.to(tl.int64) * stride_row
+    j = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    local_start = tl.maximum(num_blocks - local_blocks, 0)
+    # A block that is both init and local ends up local; the two stores below
+    # touch disjoint blocks.
+    value = tl.where(j >= local_start, SENTINEL_LOCAL, SENTINEL_INIT)
+    tl.store(score_row + j, value, mask=(j < init_blocks) & (j < num_blocks))
+    local_block = local_start + j
+    tl.store(
+        score_row + local_block,
+        SENTINEL_LOCAL,
+        mask=(j < local_blocks)
+        & (local_block < num_blocks)
+        & (local_block >= init_blocks),
+    )
+
+
+def _pin_forced_blocks(
+    score: torch.Tensor,  # [H, rows, width] fp32
+    *,
+    init_blocks: int,
+    local_blocks: int,
+    seq_lens: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    query_len: int = 1,
+    num_valid_pages: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Write AITER's init / local sentinels on the causal blocks of every row.
+
+    Decode rows are recovered from ``seq_lens`` and ``query_len``, prefill rows
+    carry their block counts in ``num_valid_pages``.
+    """
+    heads, rows, _ = score.shape
+    if rows == 0 or init_blocks + local_blocks == 0:
+        return
+    _pin_forced_blocks_kernel[(rows, heads)](
+        score,
+        seq_lens if seq_lens is not None else num_valid_pages,
+        num_valid_pages if num_valid_pages is not None else seq_lens,
+        score.stride(0),
+        score.stride(1),
+        query_len,
+        init_blocks,
+        local_blocks,
+        DECODE=seq_lens is not None,
+        BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(max(init_blocks, local_blocks)),
+        BLOCK_SIZE=MSA_SPARSE_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        SENTINEL_INIT=SENTINEL_INIT,
+        SENTINEL_LOCAL=SENTINEL_LOCAL,
+    )

+class MiniMaxM3IndexerMxfp4Metadata(MiniMaxM3IndexerMSAMetadata):

+class MiniMaxM3IndexerMxfp4MetadataBuilder(MiniMaxM3IndexerMSAMetadataBuilder):
+    """The decode scorer's work map lives in one persistent buffer.
+
+    A captured decode graph bakes in the work map's address and its row count
+    (the scorer's grid). Both therefore have to survive every replay: the map is
+    refilled in place each step, and is always built for the model-length block
+    bound, which is also the bound the graph is captured with (the model runner
+    captures with ``max_seq_len == max_model_len``).
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        kv_cache_spec: AttentionSpec,
+        layer_names: list[str],
+        vllm_config: VllmConfig,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(kv_cache_spec, layer_names, vllm_config, device)
+        self.num_index_heads = 1
+        self.max_model_len = vllm_config.model_config.max_model_len
+        self._max_decode_reqs = vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_seqs
+        self._work_map_buf: torch.Tensor | None = None
+
+    def _work_map_buffer(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if self._work_map_buf is None:
+            from aiter.ops.flydsl import minimax_m3_index_score_work_map_capacity
+
+            max_block = cdiv(self.max_model_len, self.sparse_block_size)
+            # The exact grid is not monotonic in the batch or the query length,
+            # so size for the capacity of every decode query length.
+            rows = max(
+                minimax_m3_index_score_work_map_capacity(
+                    self._max_decode_reqs, max_block, query_len, self.num_index_heads
+                )
+                for query_len in range(1, self.max_decode_query_len + 1)
+            )
+            self._work_map_buf = torch.empty(
+                (rows, 2), dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device
+            )
+        return self._work_map_buf
+
+    def build(
+        self,
+        common_prefix_len: int,
+        common_attn_metadata: CommonAttentionMetadata,
+        fast_build: bool = False,
+    ) -> MiniMaxM3IndexerMxfp4Metadata:
+        metadata = super().build(common_prefix_len, common_attn_metadata, fast_build)
+        work_map = None
+        d = metadata.decode
+        if d is not None:
+            from aiter.ops.flydsl import minimax_m3_index_score_work_map
+
+            # The scorer's block bound is part of its grid: a replayed graph
+            # keeps the one it was captured with, so every step uses it.
+            d = replace(d, max_seq_len=self.max_model_len)
+            metadata.decode = d
+            work_map = minimax_m3_index_score_work_map(
+                d.seq_lens,
+                cdiv(d.max_seq_len, self.sparse_block_size),
+                d.decode_query_len,
+                self.num_index_heads,
+                out=self._work_map_buffer(),
+            )
+        return MiniMaxM3IndexerMxfp4Metadata(
+            **{f.name: getattr(metadata, f.name) for f in fields(metadata)},
+            decode_work_map=work_map,
+        )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Page geometry of the MiniMax M3 MXFP4 K/V and index-K caches on ROCm.
+
+One 128-token page of one head holds, for K (or V, or the index key), the
+128-wide rows as e2m1 data (two elements a byte, the low nibble the even one)
+followed by one e8m0 scale per 32 elements::
+
+    [128 tokens x 64 B data][128 tokens x 4 B scale]  = 8704 B = 128 x 68 B
+
+There is no global scale. This is the page AITER's ``fused_qknorm_idxrqknorm``
+writes and its FlyDSL scorers and ``pa_decode`` (MXFP4 K/V) read.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+PAGE_TOKENS = 128
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+DATA_BYTES = HEAD_DIM // 2
+SCALE_BYTES = HEAD_DIM // 32
+# Bytes per token and per page of one head.
+TOKEN_BYTES = DATA_BYTES + SCALE_BYTES
+PAGE_BYTES = PAGE_TOKENS * TOKEN_BYTES
+
+
+def mxfp4_page_views(pages: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """(data, scale) views of uint8 pages ``[..., PAGE_BYTES]``.
+
+    The views are ``[..., 128, 64]`` and ``[..., 128, 4]`` and keep the leading
+    dims and their strides, so ``[pages, heads, 8704]`` becomes the
+    ``[pages, heads, 128, 64]`` / ``[pages, heads, 128, 4]`` pair
+    ``pa_decode`` takes and ``[pages, 8704]`` the ``[pages, 128, 64]`` /
+    ``[pages, 128, 4]`` pair the index scorers take.
+    """
+    if pages.dtype != torch.uint8 or pages.shape[-1] != PAGE_BYTES:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"MXFP4 pages are uint8 [..., {PAGE_BYTES}], got {pages.dtype} "
+            f"{tuple(pages.shape)}"
+        )
+    if pages.stride(-1) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("MXFP4 pages need a contiguous byte axis")
+    lead, lead_strides = tuple(pages.shape[:-1]), tuple(pages.stride()[:-1])
+    offset = pages.storage_offset()
+    data = pages.as_strided(
+        (*lead, PAGE_TOKENS, DATA_BYTES), (*lead_strides, DATA_BYTES, 1), offset
+    )
+    scale = pages.as_strided(
+        (*lead, PAGE_TOKENS, SCALE_BYTES),
+        (*lead_strides, SCALE_BYTES, 1),
+        offset + PAGE_TOKENS * DATA_BYTES,
+    )
+    return data, scale

+"""MiniMax M3 block-sparse attention over an MXFP4 K/V cache on ROCm (gfx950).

Pushed 91d7ee1a24 (one fast-forward commit on top of d6dbccaac4): the MXFP4 sparse attend now calls aiter's `pa_decode(out, q, k_data, v_data, ctx, bt, scale, 1, key_scale=, value_scale=, work_plan=None, max_context_length=)` instead of `aiter.ops.flydsl.pa_decode_mxfp4`; `max_partitions=1` is dropped (a plan-free call already runs one task per row). `rocm_mxfp4_aiter_unavailable_reason` probes `pa_decode` instead of the removed module, and the `mxfp4_pages` docstrings are updated. Only `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/{sparse_attention_mxfp4,indexer_mxfp4,ops/mxfp4_pages}.py` changed.

Why: ROCm/aiter#7056 (head f017c23591) merges the standalone `pa_decode_mxfp4` entry into `pa_decode` at the review's request; without this commit the availability probe reports the MXFP4 ops unavailable and the sparse path cannot run once #7056 lands. **Depends on ROCm/aiter#7056.**

Tested on gfx950 against aiter#7056 f017c23591 (same PA files), from an archive of this commit overlaid on the vllm nightly rocm100 image (0.32.0rc1, torch 2.13; python overlay, not a source build): `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_mxfp4.py -k sparse_attend`, 6 passed; ruff and ruff format clean.
